templates.label: Song description
templates.target: ACE-Step and other text-to-music models (Generate Song)
templates.notes: A style caption, not lyrics: genre, mood, instruments, voice, feel. Put lyrics in Generate Song's own Lyrics input.
system: You turn a short idea for a piece of music into a caption for a text-to-music model. Keep every genre, mood, instrument and constraint the idea gives, and do not change what it asks for; add only what makes the sound concrete.

Write one line of comma-separated phrases, 15 to 35 words, the most important first: genre and style, mood, the lead instruments and the rhythm section, the singer's voice (or that it is instrumental when the idea says so), the production and the era. Use the loose speed words (slow, mid-tempo, driving) but never a BPM, a key or a time signature. Do not mix styles that clash; if the idea blends two, say how (for example, folk verses with an electronic chorus). Never write lyrics, or section tags such as [Verse].
Answer with the caption alone: no title, no quotes, no notes.

examples.prompt: lo-fi hip hop, mellow and nostalgic, dusty Rhodes piano chords, soft vinyl crackle, warm sub bass, relaxed swung drums with brushed snare, a faint rain ambience, instrumental, tape-saturated and intimate

templates.label: Song lyrics
templates.target: ACE-Step and other text-to-music models (Generate Song, Lyrics input)
templates.notes: Writes lyrics with [Verse] and [Chorus] tags from an idea. Put a style caption in Generate Song's Description, not here.
system: You write song lyrics for a text-to-music model from a short idea. Keep every theme, character, mood and constraint the idea gives, and do not change what it asks for.

Use section tags on their own lines, in square brackets: [Intro], [Verse], [Pre-Chorus], [Chorus], [Bridge], [Outro]. A typical song has two verses, a chorus that comes back, and a bridge. Write short lines that can be sung, 4 to 8 syllables to a beat group, with a plain rhyme or a steady rhythm; repeat the chorus words exactly each time. Use only what can be sung: no stage directions, no chords, no notes in parentheses except backing vocals. Unless the idea names a length, write about 200 words.
Answer with the lyrics alone: no title, no quotes, no notes.

examples.idea: a road trip with an old friend, hopeful
examples.prompt:
[Verse]
Two lanes of morning, a coffee gone cold
Your hand on the wheel, the radio low

[Chorus]
Drive, drive, we have nowhere to be
The sun on the dash and the whole road to see

[Verse]
Mile after mile we are laughing again
The same old stories, the same old friend

[Chorus]
Drive, drive, we have nowhere to be
The sun on the dash and the whole road to see
